quarterly_data.signal: FPL 2026-2035 Ten Year Site Plan (filed with the Florida PSC): FPL's load projections assume demand from large load customers materializes starting in 2028 and reaches a peak demand of 3 GW by 2035, and the resource plan factors in that load. FPL states that there are currently no definitive agreements or other binding commitments between FPL and any large power users, but based on discussions with potential large power users it believes there is a high probability of such customers being served beginning in 2028, with total load growing to approximately 3 GW by 2035. Industrial energy sales (3.5% of 2026 sales) are projected to grow at an average annual rate of 21.1% over the forecast period, adjusted for these high load factor customers. FPL's forecast summer peak demand rises from 28,868 MW (2026) to 35,623 MW (2035) against installed capacity of 33,205 MW and 41,657 MW; the plan adds approximately 12,293 MW of new solar in 2026-2035, for approximately 20,225 MW of installed utility solar by the end of 2035.
